stories.title: New York City’s Next Multifamily Shortage? Buildings to Buy.
stories.excerpt: For years, nearly every conversation about New York City multifamily has centered around one shortage: housing. We don’t have enough apartments. We don’t build fast enough. Vacancy remains tight, construction is expensive, and the regulatory environment makes adding new supply increasingly difficult. But there is another shortage developing that investors and owners should be paying close attention to: a shortage of multifamily buildings to buy. I am talking about quality buildings worth buying — free-market apartment buildings with minimal regulatory risk hurdles. Lev Mavashev. PHOTO: Courtesy Alpha Realty That may sound strange after several years when buyers had the upper hand and plenty of owners struggled to get their pricing. But the market is changing. Capital is coming back faster than quality inventory is coming to market, and the numbers are starting to reflect that. According to Alpha Realty’s second-quarter 2026 multifamily market report, New York City recorded 304 multifamily transactions during the three months ended June 30, up 10.5 percent from the first quarter and 2.4 percent year-over-year. That followed 275 transactions in the first quarter, which itself was up nearly 20 percent from the prior year. In other words, despite elevated borrowing costs, transaction velocity continues to improve. Most of the multifamily transactions have been for free-market and newer construction buildings. What’s interesting is that multifamily buildings with 20-plus units accounted for 112 transactions in the second quarter, up 24.4 percent from the quarter before and 8.7 percent from a year earlier. Those assets represented $872.2 million, or roughly 57 percent of all New York City multifamily dollar volume during the quarter. That follows an already strong first quarter, when properties with at least 20 units accounted for $1.06 billion, or approximately 61 percent of citywide multifamily volume. bullets: NYC multifamily transactions: 304 in Q2 2026, up 10.5% QoQ and 2.4% YoY.
Capital returning faster than quality free-market inventory coming to market.
Shortage of buyable buildings with minimal regulatory risk now emerging in NYC.
stories.summary: New York City multifamily deal volume is accelerating—304 transactions in Q2 2026 versus 275 in Q1—signaling renewed investor appetite. However, the market is experiencing a reverse dynamic: capital is flowing back into the sector faster than quality, regulatory-light apartment buildings are being listed for sale. This inversion of supply and demand for assets is beginning to compress pricing and availability windows.
stories.impact: This signals a tightening acquisition window for NYC multifamily developers and investors. As capital returns and deals move faster, land and portfolio costs will likely rise before new supply can be built. Developers holding entitled sites or in predevelopment should prioritize financing and underwriting to move ahead of rising basis costs; conversely, those without land should expect competitive bidding and repricing upward across Manhattan, Queens, and the Bronx.

stories.title: AI-Searched Public Records Alone Insufficient for Title Decision-Making: Study
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence-only searches of public records aren’t enough to provide reliable title decision-making at scale, according to a new study by DataTrace, a national provider of property and ownership data and title automation solutions. The company’s analysis, “AI Title Search Tested in the Real World: What Accuracy, Risk and Readiness Really Look Like,” compares AI-only with title plant-supported searches to evaluate completeness, accuracy and insurability. (A title plant is an index of all of the recorded events that affect a property, unique in that it’s posted, or indexed, as the official legal description of the property.) “The study is a projection of potential risk, and the opportunity to look at specific — what we would call, gaps — where the AI solution alone was used,” said Annette Cotton, senior vice president and chief data officer at DataTrace. “It predicts if that property had been insured upon, for instance, what could have been an outcome in terms of not being able to report on, address, or remediate that gap. “Our analysis demonstrates that AI performs best when it operates on a foundation of structured, validated title data, rather than fragmented county-level public records. The speed of AI creates value, but only when paired with the confidence, completeness and accuracy needed for insurable title decisioning. The future isn’t AI versus title professionals. It’s AI powered by trusted title data and guided by experienced title experts. That’s how the industry scales automation without sacrificing confidence or insurability.” DataTrace manages more than 2,000 title plants nationally. The new study is a follow-up to DataTrace’s first white paper on its position concerning title plant value, said Cotton. “This was intended to try to answer more details about that and what the impact would have been based on those early findings when we were doing the AI testing against traditional examination.” Among the current study’s
bullets: DataTrace study shows AI-only title searches insufficient for reliable insurance decisions.
AI performs best on structured, valid data; gaps remain when used alone.
Title plants (recorded legal indexes) still required to supplement AI for completeness.
stories.summary: A DataTrace analysis comparing AI-only versus title plant-supported searches found that artificial intelligence alone cannot reliably identify all recorded events and liens affecting a property. AI performs well on structured data but creates gaps in edge cases, creating potential title insurance exposure. The study underscores that AI title automation requires a human-curated, indexed foundation to be viable at scale.
stories.impact: For multifamily developers acquiring land or portfolios, this means due diligence timelines may not compress as much as proptech vendors promise. Relying on AI-only title searches risks uninsurable gaps that could delay closings or create post-acquisition liability. Budget for hybrid human-AI title review, especially in complex markets (NYC, DC) where recorded histories are deep and title defects more common.

stories.title: SFR Leasing Operating System Boom Secures $15M Series A Funding
stories.excerpt: Boom, a leasing operating system for single family rentals (SFR), announced Tuesday that it has secured $15 million in Series A funding. The company also announced the launch of BoomCRM, an agentic leasing and touring customer relationship management product built on top of the Boom’s existing underwriting engine. S3 Ventures led the round, with Mischief VC (fund of Plaid CEO Zach Perret) participating. Repeat participation came from venture capital firms Starting Line VC, Company Ventures, and Gilgamesh Ventures. Founded in 2020 and based in Austin, Texas, Boom bills itself as a financial services infrastructure company for rental operations. It works with property management systems dealing with on-time payments, fraud reduction and revenue growth across the renter lifecycle for SFR, scattered site and manufactured housing (MH) sectors. “We have been fairly conservative to date on the capital we’ve raised and the capital we’ve spent,” said Rob Whiting, CEO and co-founder at Boom. “We have a strong product market fit and have grown about 8x up until our Series A, and we’ve further grown 3x since the start of the year. This funding will help us accelerate several things, including the launch of this product and several more products after this, as well as growing the engineering team to support that, along with go-to-market efforts. As we primarily play in single-family rentals and manufactured housing, we want to continue to double down in those areas.” Boom’s existing products are BoomReport, automated rent reporting to incentivize on-time payments, grow revenue, and build resident credit, and BoomScreen, a tenant screening tool to mitigate fraud, increase leasing velocity, and move in best-qualified renters. Whiting said that most leasing CRMs today are either built multifamily-first or are general-purpose tools such as Salesforce and HubSpot, retrofitted for rentals. bullets: Boom (SFR leasing OS) raises $15M Series A led by S3 Ventures.
Company grown 8x before round; additional 3x growth post-Series A.
Platform serves SFR, scattered-site, and manufactured housing underwriting and collections.
stories.summary: Boom, an Austin-based leasing and financial services operating system for single-family rentals, secured $15 million in Series A funding to expand its underwriting, fraud-reduction, and CRM tools. The company has achieved strong product-market fit (8x pre-Series A growth, 3x post-Series A), positioning itself as infrastructure for fragmented SFR portfolios and scattered-site operators.
stories.impact: This reflects institutional capital's confidence in the SFR and scattered-site sectors as alternatives to traditional multifamily development. For multifamily operators considering SFR bolt-ons or alternative rental models, Boom's funding signals a maturing fintech ecosystem that can reduce friction in lease execution and collections, improving IRRs on smaller-unit portfolios. Monitor SFR-focused fintech vendors as potential acquisition targets or operational partners for portfolio scaling.

stories.title: Atrium Launches AI Platform, Tracking $1.3T of U.S. Data Center Development Credit
stories.excerpt: The data center marketplace keeps growing, and one analytics firm has tracked where all $1.3 trillion of identifiable debt powering this development boom of nearly 4,300 U.S. data centers has come from — and where it is going. Commercial Observer can first report that Atrium, a San Diego-based AI analytics startup founded in 2024, has launched its new interactive data and research platform, “Who Finances America’s Data Centers,” to track the debt dollars behind every data center deal in the U.S. The platform is a first-of-its-kind resource that uses data collated from local property records, SEC credit agreements, commercial mortgage-backed security (CMBS) securitizations, as well as commercial bank and private credit loan syndications and corporate debt issuances to follow the money behind 3,038 operational data center deals — and another 1,258 that are in different stages of their lifecycles. Ryan Alfred, founder at Atrium Data, told CO that “data centers are the biggest driver in the economy right now,” but because they’re financed differently than traditional real estate classes — and often require layers of county-level loans, syndicated debt, CMBS, asset-backed securities, SPV structures, and, most unusually, credit issued by regional utility companies — it has been difficult for market players to get a clear picture on the debt behind the boom. “As a result, no one had this 360-degree view of who is financing them and what their credit structures are,” he said. “We went out and used all our data, and all our resources, to build the 360-degree vehicle of data center financings.” The firm’s website notes that the tool and report are “the first in an ongoing series that will track every identifiable data center investment dollar in the United States” and that it will be updated periodically as deals close, including securitizations and county-level recordings. bullets: Atrium launches AI platform tracking $1.3T in U.S. data center debt across 4,300 sites.
Platform covers 3,038 operational and 1,258 in-pipeline data center deals.
Debt sourced from local records, SEC filings, CMBS, bank syndications, and corporate issuance.
stories.summary: Atrium, a 2024-founded AI analytics startup, launched an interactive platform cataloging $1.3 trillion in identifiable debt financing nearly 4,300 U.S. data centers, including 3,038 operational and 1,258 in-development facilities. The tool aggregates data from property records, CMBS securitizations, bank loans, and corporate debt to track capital flow and financing patterns across the sector.
stories.impact: Data center development is consuming significant capital and land in major metros (Virginia, Northern California, Dallas, Phoenix). Multifamily developers should monitor data center concentration in target markets—these uses compete for land, drive up ground lease costs, and can depress or elevate residential demand depending on job creation and wage intensity. Understanding local data center pipelines helps inform whether a market faces residential supply headwinds (land scarcity) or tailwinds (job growth from cloud/AI tenants).

stories.title: Corpay’s Cross-Border Business Leases Prebuilt at Rudin’s 560 Lexington
stories.excerpt: Rudin announced a new 11-year office lease with Corpay, Inc.’s. Cross-Border business at 560 Lexington Ave., its 22-story office tower in the Plaza District. Corpay Cross-Border Solutions, which specializes in foreign exchange, global payments and risk management, will relocate its headquarters to 560 Lexington this fall. The company will occupy a 17,778-square-foot prebuilt space spanning the entire 17th floor of the 380,000-square-foot building. “Corpay’s commitment to 560 Lexington demonstrates the continued allure of the Plaza District and further validates our investments in our portfolio’s amenity and prebuild programs,” said Kevin Daly, VP of office leasing at Rudin. “Given these ongoing efforts, only minor modifications to a prebuilt floor were needed to meet Corpay’s requirements. This allowed us to accommodate their accelerated timeline for move-in, which was a big factor in getting the deal done.” Jacob Rosenthal and Kevin Carroll of CBRE represented Corpay. Rudin was represented in-house by Daly and a CBRE team of Peter Turchin, Brett Shannon, Eric Deutsch and Lauren Levy. The post Corpay’s Cross-Border Business Leases Prebuilt at Rudin’s 560 Lexington appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Corpay Cross-Border relocates NYC HQ to 560 Lexington Ave, Plaza District.
11-year lease for 17,778 sf on entire 17th floor; move-in fall 2025.
Rudin leveraged prebuilt floor to accelerate tenant move-in and close deal.
stories.summary: Corpay Cross-Border Solutions, a foreign exchange and global payments company, signed an 11-year lease to relocate its headquarters to a prebuilt 17,778-square-foot floor at Rudin's 560 Lexington Ave. in Manhattan's Plaza District. The deal validates Rudin's amenity and prebuild strategy in attracting quality tenants with accelerated timelines.
stories.impact: This is an office lease, not multifamily, but signals persistent Plaza District / Midtown Manhattan demand from financial services and payment tech firms. Such corporate relocations can anchor residential demand in nearby areas (Murray Hill, Kips Bay, Plaza) if the company brings 200+ employees. Monitor whether Corpay or similar fintech/payments firms expand headcount in NYC, as that drives ancillary demand for luxury rentals and could support nearby multifamily development or conversions.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap’s Azzi Group Closes Value-Add Sale of West Hollywood Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 1203 N. Kings Road, a 30-unit multifamily property in West Hollywood. The property sold for $7.98 million, or $266,000 per unit. “The property presented the buyer with a rare opportunity to acquire a well-located West Hollywood asset at an attractive basis with significant value-add potential,” said Tony Azzi, executive managing director investments. “With opportunities to renovate vacant units and improve operations, the buyer is well positioned to enhance the property’s long-term cash flow. West Hollywood continues to benefit from strong rental demand driven by limited housing supply, walkability and access to major employment and lifestyle destinations throughout Los Angeles,” added Rabbie Banafsheha, senior director investments. Azzi and Banafsheha, of The Azzi Group in Marcus & Millichap’s Los Angeles office, marketed the property on behalf of the seller. Azzi, Banafsheha, Arteen Zahiri and Ian Habbestad, also of The Azzi Group, procured the buyer. The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. The post Marcus & Millichap’s Azzi Group Closes Value-Add Sale of West Hollywood Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: West Hollywood 30-unit property sold for $7.98M ($266K/unit) via Marcus & Millichap.
Value-add play: vacant units + operational improvements driving returns.
Buyer attracted by limited supply, walkability, and strong rental demand in WeHo.
stories.summary: The Azzi Group at Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 1203 N. Kings Road, a 30-unit West Hollywood multifamily asset, for $7.98 million or $266,000 per unit. The buyer is executing a value-add strategy renovating vacant units and improving operations, capitalizing on West Hollywood's limited housing supply, walkability, and proximity to LA employment and lifestyle hubs.
stories.impact: West Hollywood multifamily valuations remain elevated on scarcity and quality-of-life factors. The $266K/unit basis signals a tight supply-demand dynamic in a submarket where new construction is heavily restricted. Developers with land or conversion opportunities in WeHo or adjacent LA submarkets (Beverly Hills, Hollywood, Los Feliz) should prioritize entitlements and financing, as the value-add buyer willingness and limited competing supply support strong IRRs.

stories.title: Northmarq Arranges $75M Acquisition Loan for Grocery-Anchored Queens Center
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s New York Debt + Equity team led by Robert Delitsky and Keith Braddish arranged a $75-million loan for the acquisition and redevelopment of Whitestone Shopping Center, a 119,584-square-foot grocery-anchored shopping center located at 153-17 Cross Island Pkwy. in Whitestone, Queens. Northmarq arranged financing on behalf of BTF Whitestone LLC after running a marketing process with the lending community. Northmarq and ownership selected Acadia Realty Trust. The principals of BTF Whitestone LLC are Aaron Malinsky and Kenneth Schuckman. “After being overlooked for decades, Whitestone Shopping Center is about to undergo a significant transformation that will benefit both its tenants and the surrounding community,” said Delitsky. “Kenneth Schuckman and Aaron Malinsky are the ideal developers to restore Whitestone Shopping Center into a vibrant neighborhood retail destination.” The center is anchored by Key Food Supermarket, with additional tenants including Webster Bank and JPMorgan Chase. The post Northmarq Arranges $75M Acquisition Loan for Grocery-Anchored Queens Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Northmarq arranges $75M acquisition/redevelopment loan for Whitestone Shopping Center, Queens.

stories.summary: Northmarq's New York team arranged a $75 million acquisition and redevelopment loan for Whitestone Shopping Center, a 119,584-square-foot grocery-anchored retail property in Queens anchored by Key Food. Acadia Realty Trust provided the financing to BTF Whitestone LLC, which plans a significant repositioning of an underutilized asset.
stories.impact: Neighborhood retail redevelopments in outer-borough Queens (Whitestone) signal capital appetite for value-add retail with ancillary residential upside. Developers should assess whether Whitestone or similar Queens retail corridors (Astoria, Forest Hills, Rego Park) can support mixed-use or multifamily-anchored projects. Underperforming retail in residential neighborhoods often offers land/air-rights opportunities when redeveloped with apartments; monitor Acadia's Whitestone strategy for nearby multifamily development signals.

stories.title: SRS Arranges Sale of Newly Built Caliber Collision Property
stories.excerpt: SRS Real Estate Partners has completed the $5.24-million sale of a Caliber Collision property located at 742 Main Street in Chula Vista. The 16,832-square-foot property recently completed construction and has a 15-year corporate-guaranteed absolute triple net lease in place. SRS Capital Markets senior managing principals Matthew Mousavi and Patrick Luther and VP Greg Labarre represented the seller, a Southern California-based developer. The buyer was a family trust from Southern California. The property is part of a new development that will feature Starbucks, Quick Quack Car Wash, Taco Bell, Circle K and Chipotle, among other recognizable brands, all separately marketed and available for sale by SRS with a total value of approximately $30 million. It is less than a mile from Interstate 805 and Chula Vista Crossings, a Kohl’s-anchored retail center. “This property had a significant amount of investor interest and sold over the asking price, which was a 5.5% cap rate,” said Luther. “This long-term tenant is poised to do significant business as it is located near multiple auto dealerships and auto service retailers and is in a densely populated area with more than 348,200 residents, and 81,200 employees within a one-mile radius.” Mousavi added, “This was an ideal, fee-simple, low-maintenance opportunity for the new owner as it presents minimal property management responsibilities.” The post SRS Arranges Sale of Newly Built Caliber Collision Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: SRS completes $5.24M sale of Caliber Collision property, Chula Vista, CA.
16,832 sf; 15-year corporate-guaranteed NNN lease at 5.5% cap rate.
New mixed-use development near I-805; $30M total project value with Starbucks, QQC, Taco Bell anchors.
stories.summary: SRS Real Estate Partners sold a newly built 16,832-square-foot Caliber Collision property in Chula Vista for $5.24 million on a 15-year corporate-guaranteed triple-net lease at a 5.5% cap rate. The property is part of a larger $30 million mixed-use development near Interstate 805, featuring multiple national retail anchors (Starbucks, Quick Quack, Taco Bell, Circle K, Chipotle).
stories.impact: Chula Vista's dense population (348K within 1 mile) and auto-centric retail development signal growing residential demand in San Diego's South County. Multifamily developers should monitor Chula Vista / South Bay San Diego for infill and mixed-use opportunities near retail nodes and transit; these mixed-use hubs often support adjacent apartment projects. The 5.5% cap rate on NNN retail reflects investor confidence in the submarket's fundamentals.

stories.title: NAI Hanson Tapped to Lease Former Barnes & Noble Headquarters
stories.excerpt: NAI James E. Hanson announced that SVPs W. Joshua Levering, SIOR, and Charles Laginestra, and associate Chris D’Andrea, have been tapped by First National Realty Management, LLC, as the exclusive leasing team for 120 Mountainview Blvd. in Basking Ridge, NJ. The former world headquarters of Barnes & Noble, 120 Mountainview features a two-story lobby, an onsite cafe, outdoor seating, a bocce court, over 500 on-site parking spaces, and more. The property also offers a location near Interstates 78 and 287, providing access to Newark Liberty International Airport, New York City and Somerset County’s corporate corridor. “This is a rare opportunity to secure a large block of Class-A space in one of the state’s most established corporate corridors,” said Levering. “With new ownership that is experienced and fully committed to reinvesting in the property, 120 Mountainview is perfectly suited for users seeking a striking headquarters that offers flexibility, connectivity, responsive ownership, and a full suite of premium amenities.” The post NAI Hanson Tapped to Lease Former Barnes & Noble Headquarters appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NAI Hanson leasing former Barnes & Noble HQ at 120 Mountainview Blvd, Basking Ridge, NJ.
Class-A office in Somerset County corporate corridor near I-78, I-287, Newark airport.
Two-story lobby, onsite cafe, 500+ parking; rare large block of premium space.
stories.summary: NAI James E. Hanson was appointed exclusive leasing agent for 120 Mountainview Boulevard, the former Barnes & Noble world headquarters in Basking Ridge, New Jersey. The Class-A office property features premium amenities and connectivity to Interstate 78, 287, Newark Liberty airport, and the corporate corridor, positioning it for large-block tenants.
stories.impact: This is an office lease, not multifamily, but Basking Ridge and Somerset County corporate corridor are key employment hubs for North Jersey multifamily demand. If 120 Mountainview successfully leases to large tenants (tech, finance, pharma), it signals sustained job growth and could support new multifamily development in nearby areas (Bernardsville, Gladstone, Bedminster). Monitor Somerset County employment trends as a leading indicator for residential demand.

stories.title: Starwood Lands $483M CMBS Loan to Refi Single-Family Rental Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management secured a $482.5 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan to refinance a nearly full single-family rental portfolio located across 10 states. The floating-rate, interest-only financing — which Japan’s Nomura Securities originated — backs 1,749 properties, according to Fitch Ratings. The debt, which is scheduled to mature in August 2028, has three 12-month extension options. The portfolio was just over 96 percent leased in April. On average, the homes span 1,812 square feet and date back to 1992. Starwood Asset Management paid $674 million for the houses, assembling the portfolio between 2021 and 2022. Nearly a third are located in Georgia, followed by nearly a quarter in Arizona and just under 12 percent in Florida. Within Palm Beach County, there are 27 homes, most of which are located in Lake Worth, according to property records. The debt comes as Starwood has been making other multifamily inroads, buying four affordable housing properties across Miami-Dade County just last week for a combined $115 million. For Nomura, the financing marks a sizable loan since re-entering the U.S. market last year after a 27-year hiatus. A division of Nomura Group, one of Japan’s major financial institutions, the firm had helped pioneer the CMBS scheme back in the 1990s. Representatives for Starwood declined to comment, while representatives for Nomura did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management secures $482.5M CMBS refi for 1,749-property SFR portfolio.
Portfolio: 96% leased, avg 1,812 sf, assembled 2021-22 at $674M cost.
Geographically: ~33% Georgia, ~24% Arizona, ~12% Florida; 27 in Palm Beach.
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management obtained a $482.5 million CMBS loan (originated by Nomura) to refinance a nearly fully leased single-family rental portfolio of 1,749 homes across 10 states. The homes, averaging 1,812 square feet and built around 1992, were assembled between 2021 and 2022 for $674 million, with concentrations in Georgia, Arizona, and Florida.
stories.impact: Starwood's SFR securitization signals strong CMBS appetite for stabilized, diversified SFR portfolios—a trend favoring larger operators and potentially raising exit multiples for smaller SFR portfolios. For multifamily developers, this underscores institutional capital's confidence in rental housing at scale. The Georgia, Arizona, and Florida concentrations mirror multifamily supply constraints in those Sunbelt markets; monitor whether SFR bulk acquisitions are outpacing multifamily land availability, as that signals continued scarcity and support for apartment development fundamentals.
